_meta.note: Substitutions work best in most recipes but can affect texture. Never guarantee allergy-safe substitutions.
_meta.disclaimer: Sam offers substitutions as a starting point. Not medical or allergy advice.

free.substitute: 1 cup milk + 1 tablespoon white vinegar or lemon juice. Stir and let sit 5 minutes.
1 tablespoon ground flaxseed + 3 tablespoons water. Mix and let sit 5 minutes to thicken.
free.notes: Works for cookies, muffins, quick breads. Not for airy or leavened bakes.
Cake will be more moist. Not ideal for cookies where creaming matters.
Cookies spread more and taste less rich.

free.substitute: 1 cup white sugar + 1 tablespoon molasses (for light) or 2 tablespoons (for dark). Mix well.
3/4 cup + 2 tablespoons all purpose flour + 2 tablespoons cornstarch. Sift twice.
free.notes: The cornstarch lowers the protein like cake flour does.

free.substitute: 1 cup all purpose flour + 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder + 1/4 teaspoon salt
free.notes: Use immediately, don't store the mix.

free.substitute: 1/4 teaspoon baking soda + 1/2 teaspoon cream of tartar

free.notes: Won't whip. Fine for sauces, ganache, baked goods.
For baking only. Won't taste right in coffee or on cereal.
Mild flavor swap. Works in most cookies and cakes.

free.substitute: 3 tablespoons cocoa powder + 1 tablespoon butter or oil
3/4 cup brown sugar + 1/4 cup water. Warm to dissolve.

free.notes: Changes color and flavor slightly. Fine for most baking.

free.substitute: There is no true substitute. For quick breads only: use baking powder or a combo of baking soda + acid.
free.notes: Real yeast breads need the real thing. Hmm.

free.substitute: 2 teaspoons lemon juice or white vinegar
free.notes: Works for meringues and some acid uses.
